# 1 Enoch Chapter 105 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 105:1 — 'I and my son' vs. 'My son and I'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I-and-my-son-will-be-joined-with-them" | Literal Ge'ez word order |
| LOGOS | "I and my son will be joined with them" | Formal; preserves Ge'ez order |
| PNEUMA | "My son and I will walk with them forever" | Reverses order; more natural English |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'I and my son.' The Ge'ez word order places the speaker first; the reversal (PNEUMA) is naturally idiomatic in English but the original emphasis is on the speaker (Enoch) as the guarantor of the promise.

---

## 105:1 — 'be joined with them' vs. 'walk with them'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "will-be-joined-with-them for-ever-in-the-paths-of-uprightness" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "will be joined with them forever in the paths of uprightness" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "will walk with them forever, side by side, on the paths of righteousness" | 'Walk with them' for 'be joined'; adds 'side by side' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'joined with them.' 'Be joined' is the Ge'ez verb — the relational union is expressed as joining, not merely walking. PNEUMA's 'walk with them side by side' is warm but 'side by side' is not in the source.

---

## 105:1 — 'children of uprightness' vs. 'children of righteousness'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "children-of-uprightness" | Literal: sedeq = uprightness/righteousness |
| LOGOS | "children of uprightness" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "children of righteousness" | 'Righteousness' for 'uprightness' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'uprightness.' The term sedeq has been consistently rendered 'uprightness' throughout the Epistle to preserve a distinction from tsedakah/dikaiosynē. Maintaining this distinction in the closing verse is important for consistency.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 3**
